newsitem.title: INDIA: Delhi shares end 2.3 pct higher on short-covering.
newsitem.headline: Delhi shares end 2.3 pct higher on short-covering.

text.p: Shares on the Delhi bourse surged on short-covering by domestic financial institutions, triggered by reports that the Finance Ministry might take measures to boost investor confidence, brokers said.
Brokers said foreign institutional investors (FIIs), which had been unloading shares in the past few sessions, helped fuel the rebound.
The Delhi Stock Exchange's sensitive index closed 14.15 points, or 2.27 percent, higher at 636.89.
"Heavy buying by domestic financial institutions mainly arrested the long bearish conditions," said Harish Malhotra of brokers Malhotra Financial Services.
The Economic Times newspaper reported that top Finance Ministry officials were to meet the heads of the three major domestic financial institutions on Friday to review the sluggish market conditions.

Brokers said the rise was partly a technical correction after several sessions of declining prices. "Huge short-covering by bear operators suggests that market was in an over-sold position," a broker said.
ACC rose 24 rupees to 943 on institutional buying, brokers said.
Reliance Industries was heavily traded throughout the day and closed 5 rupees rupees higher at 183.75.
Larsen and Toubro shot up 10.50 rupees, or 5.59 percent, to 198.50 rupees on buying by FIIs.
State Bank of India surged 5.50 rupees to 211.10, in line with the general upbeat trend.
